Potential edge cases:

lowerCase:
- null -> "" (empty)
- empty string -> ""
- string with uppercase ASCII -> lowercased
- string with mixed case
- string with locale-specific characters (e.g., "İstanbul" contains capital I with dot; in EN locale, "İ" lowercasing yields "i̇"? Actually Java's toLowerCase(Locale.ENGLISH) for "İ" returns "i̇" (i + combining dot). Might be okay. We'll test that result is as expected using known behavior. But we can just assert that result equals input.toLowerCase(Locale.ENGLISH) (i.e., same as method). Might not be needed.

normalize:
- null -> "" (lowerCase returns "", then trim => "")
- empty -> ""
- string with leading/trailing spaces -> trimmed lowercased
- string with internal spaces unchanged after lowercasing
- string with only whitespace -> "" after trim
- string with uppercase and spaces

Edge: string with newline or tab characters; trim removes leading/trailing whitespace including those.

Will use @Test annotation.

Will also test that lowerCase does not modify original string (strings immutable anyway).
